threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You believe a ‘local’ café can be found just around the corner but end up at a hipster brunch spot with a 45-minute wait.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded everyone with an out-of-tune version of 'Wonderwall' while debating the best chicken shops in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids using a street vendor's table as a makeshift stage for pop-up performances, I realized I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night döner kebab stand selling currywurst at 3 AM, all while a punk band plays on the street corner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to BART delays; they just roll their eyes and check their phone, while newcomers look panicked.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hopping on the 31. He even adjusted his bow tie before sitting down. Muni’s the real red carpet around here.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about parks and plazas, but the real charm is in the narrow streets with quirky shops that stay open late.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they struggle to order a coffee without saying 'café con leche'—locals know it's just 'café'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: If you still call it a ‘bus stop’ instead of a ‘bus shelter,’ you’re definitely new around here. Locals just know.
Last night on the 196, a guy tucked into a full fish and chips meal like it was a five-star restaurant. The smell was something else.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last Sunday, I saw a guy walking his ferret on a leash near the canal. That’s when it hit me—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a carnival-like pop-up bar in an abandoned factory, serving cocktails alongside DJ sets while graffiti artists paint live.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they side-eye BART delays; the rest just complain about late trains without knowing the real chaos of the Transbay Tube.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy practicing his stand-up routine; he didn’t miss a beat even with the bumps. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into the plaça and find a taverna; locals know that the best vermut is in the tiny bars down the side streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their confused face at the Diagonal metro station during rush hour. It’s like navigating a maze!
